key_insight: No single rubric currently evaluates all major dimensions of clinical reasoning in LLMs, so the authors propose combining multiple tools into a more complete assessment framework.
clinical_relevance: For AI medicine, this matters because strong exam accuracy alone may miss failures in problem representation, temporal synthesis, uncertainty calibration, and reasoning faithfulness across real clinical records.
method: Narrative review across three literatures: medical education rubrics, clinical LLM benchmarks since 2023, and general long-form generation evaluation.
Mapped six reasoning dimensions: problem representation, temporal synthesis, differential/management reasoning, counterfactual reasoning, calibrated uncertainty, and faithfulness.
Synthesized design recommendations such as binary rubric items, separate completeness vs correctness scores, importance weighting, safety caps, and temporal consistency checks.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes existing instruments and reports that no single tool covers all six dimensions; only one clinical causal-ablation study on faithfulness was identified.
watch_item: This is a design rationale, not a validated instrument, and some areas—especially uncertainty, counterfactual reasoning, and faithfulness over longitudinal free-text records—remain underdeveloped.
paper_title: A rubric landscape for evaluating clinical reasoning in large language models: what exists, what is missing, and what needs to be combined
